operators.meaning: Constructs a DATE_RANGE value from start and end date entity references. gotchas.text: operands are BARE entity refs, including semantic indexes: write DateRange(OrderDate, DeliveryDate) or DateRange(Items/Date For "sku1", Items/Date For SelectedSku), never bracket either operand. Brackets mark a comparison value; a function's arguments are not that, and bracketing them is MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN.

passing each construction's own endpoint gate is not enough: == and != additionally require BOTH range operands to declare the SAME date components, and so does a DATE_RANGE computation target. A yyyy construction beside a full yyyy-MM-dd range is MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE_RANGE in either authored order, and two stored ranges of different profiles draw it too. Base-year completion is excluded from this gate.

a component-omitting endpoint completes ASYMMETRICALLY, exactly as a stored range does: the start takes the earliest date its components denote and the FINISH the latest. So DateRange over two MM fields holding 06 and 09 spans 06-01 through 09-30 and equals the stored MM range 06/09; reading both endpoints as ordinary dates would make that equality never hold.

constraints: each operand is a bare entity reference whose DECLARED FORMAT carries date components and no time component — the declared KIND takes no part, so a TIME-declared or DATE_TIME-declared field carrying yyyy-MM-dd is admitted in the start position, the finish position and both at once, while a stamp-formatted DATE_TIME and a clock-formatted DATE are refused MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP. A DATE_FRAGMENT is admitted and may be mixed in. Both formats must contain the SAME date components, lexical spellings may differ, and a computation target must be a DATE_RANGE declaring those same components (Locked: rulekit.validate.laws.TemporalConstructorDeclaredFormatGateLawsTest)
